config.framing_prompt: According to the Deutsche Bundesbank, the wealthiest 10% of households in Germany hold over 60% of total net wealth, while the bottom 50% hold less than 3%. At the same time, Germany has no net wealth tax (the Vermögensteuer has been suspended since 1997) and inheritance tax revenues remain modest relative to GDP. Discuss whether the government should introduce a wealth tax, reform the inheritance tax, or pursue alternative redistribution mechanisms — and what effects such policies would have on economic growth, investment, and social cohesion. Ground your arguments in your party's documented positions.

turns.text: The CDU/CSU firmly opposes the introduction of a new wealth tax, as we believe Germany is already a high-tax jurisdiction where further burdens on capital would undermine the competitiveness of our Mittelstand and discourage the investment necessary for growth. Instead of penalizing those who build wealth, we advocate for a comprehensive tax reform that lowers the corporate tax rate on retained earnings to a maximum of 25 percent, ensuring that performance is rewarded and that our economy remains a global leader. We also support reducing the income tax burden by flattening the tax rate bracket and raising the basic tax-free allowance, which directly benefits small and medium-sized incomes. By focusing on tax relief and reducing bureaucracy, we create the fiscal space and economic stability needed to strengthen our social net from a position of strength, rather than dismantling the very engine of prosperity that funds it.
